# Review pack: Dawud

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/dawud.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The chapters are a reading order built from the ayat, not a chronology the Quran claims; surah order is not time order. The account at 21:78-79 is shared with Sulayman and appears in both drafts. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Dawud's worship and on what was given to him. None is used in this draft.
- The disputants' ayat (38:21-25) are stated as the ayat have them. The identity of the speaker in 38:24, the sense of the test and of that in 38:25, and the sense of khalifah in 38:26 are for a scholar to word; this draft gives no verdict.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: explanations of the test in 38:24 and names for the disputants. None is used and no verdict is implied.
- The chapters follow a reading order (gifts, the victory, the mountains and birds, the iron, the judgment about the field, the disputants, the trust on the earth). The Quran does not give a chronology across these surahs.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Favour and strength  (`#favour-and-strength`)

Cited ayat: 27:15, 38:17, 38:20

> **27:15** وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ عِلْمًا وَقَالَا ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

> **38:17** ٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلْأَيْدِ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ

> **38:20** وَشَدَدْنَا مُلْكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ ٱلْخِطَابِ

### Claims

**c1** (27:15): God gave Dawud and Sulayman knowledge, and they said that praise belongs to God, who had favoured them over many of His believing servants.

**c2** (38:17): The one addressed is told to be patient with what they say and to remember God's servant Dawud, who had strength and was one who turned back to God again and again.

**c3** (38:20): God made his kingdom firm and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.

### One-minute summary

God gave Dawud knowledge, wisdom and a firm kingdom, and called him a servant of strength who turned back to God again and again [c1][c2][c3].

### Complete story

God gave Dawud and Sulayman knowledge, and they said that praise belongs to God, who had favoured them over many of His believing servants [c1]. In another passage the one addressed is told to be patient with what they say and to remember God's servant Dawud, who had strength and was one who turned back to God again and again [c2]. God made his kingdom firm and gave him wisdom and decisive speech [c3].

### Deep study

In 27:15 the words of thanks are said by Dawud and Sulayman together, and the favour is named as God's favour [c1]. The Arabic word for strength in 38:17 is ayd, and awwab means one who turns back again and again [c2]. The phrase rendered decisive speech is fasl al-khitab, and the ayah does not fix its sense [c3].

### Kids mode

God gave Dawud knowledge and wisdom and made his kingdom strong [c1][c3]. God called him a servant who kept turning back to God [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): In 27:15 the answer to the gift of knowledge is thanks to God [c1]. A reader may notice that 38:17 joins strength and turning back to God in one description [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the knowledge given to Dawud and Sulayman consisted of; the ayah says only that it was knowledge.
- Not established: who the speakers are in 38:17 whose words the one addressed must bear with; the ayah does not name them.
- Not established: the exact sense of decisive speech (fasl al-khitab) in 38:20; the ayah does not say, and the reviewer decides the wording.

## 2. The kingdom and Jalut  (`#the-kingdom-and-jalut`)

Cited ayat: 2:251

> **2:251** فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُۥدُ جَالُوتَ وَءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُلْكَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:251): By God's permission they routed them, and Dawud killed Jalut.

**c2** (2:251): God gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him of what He willed.

**c3** (2:251): Were it not for God's driving back of people, some by means of others, the earth would be ruined, but God is full of bounty to all the worlds.

### One-minute summary

By God's permission they routed them and Dawud killed Jalut, and God gave him the kingdom and wisdom [c1][c2].

### Complete story

By God's permission they routed them, and Dawud killed Jalut [c1]. God gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him of what He willed [c2]. The verse adds that were it not for God's driving back of people, some by means of others, the earth would be ruined, but God is full of bounty to all the worlds [c3].

### Deep study

The verse does not name those who routed or those who were routed; its pronouns look back to the verses before it [c1]. It lists the kingdom, wisdom and teaching from what God willed as gifts to Dawud [c2]. The last clause turns from this event to a general statement about God's driving back of people [c3].

### Kids mode

By God's permission Dawud killed Jalut [c1]. God gave Dawud a kingdom and wisdom [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The verse places the victory under God's permission and names the kingdom and wisdom as gifts from God [c1][c2]. It also joins this event to a wider statement that God drives people back by means of one another so that the earth is not ruined [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how Jalut was killed, or Dawud's age, rank or place in the host; the verse says only that he killed him.
- Not established here: who led those who routed Jalut's side; that account lies in the verses before 2:251, outside the range of this draft.
- Not established: what the things were that God taught him from what He willed.

## 3. The mountains and the birds  (`#mountains-and-birds`)

Cited ayat: 21:79, 34:10, 38:18-19

> **21:79** فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ

> **34:10** وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًا يَٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِى مَعَهُۥ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ

> **38:18** إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا ٱلْجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ وَٱلْإِشْرَاقِ
>
> **38:19** وَٱلطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً كُلٌّ لَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ

### Claims

**c1** (21:79): God made the mountains subject to Dawud, glorifying God with him, and the birds as well.

**c2** (34:10): God gave Dawud favour from Himself and told the mountains, and the birds, to turn back with him.

**c3** (38:18-19): God made the mountains subject to him, glorifying God in the evening and at sunrise, and the birds were gathered, each of them one who turned back.

### One-minute summary

The mountains and the birds were made subject to Dawud and glorified God with him [c1][c3].

### Complete story

God made the mountains subject to Dawud, glorifying God with him, and the birds as well [c1]. God gave Dawud favour from Himself and told the mountains, and the birds, to turn back with him [c2]. God made the mountains subject to him, glorifying God in the evening and at sunrise, and the birds were gathered, each of them one who turned back [c3].

### Deep study

The ayat use different verbs: glorify in 21:79 and 38:18, turn back with him in 34:10, and gathered in 38:19 [c1][c2][c3]. The times named in 38:18 are the evening and sunrise [c3].

### Kids mode

The mountains and the birds praised God together with Dawud [c1][c3]. God told them to join him [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): In these ayat creation is shown joining in the glorifying of God [c1][c3]. A reader may notice that the birds are described as gathered and each one as turning back [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how the mountains and the birds glorified, or what it sounded like; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: whether the words each of them one who turned back point to Dawud or to God; the Arabic is open and the reviewer decides.
- Not established: where or how often this happened, beyond the evening and sunrise named in 38:18.

## 4. Iron and protection  (`#iron-and-protection`)

Cited ayat: 34:10-11, 21:80

> **34:10** وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًا يَٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِى مَعَهُۥ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ
>
> **34:11** أَنِ ٱعْمَلْ سَٰبِغَٰتٍ وَقَدِّرْ فِى ٱلسَّرْدِ وَٱعْمَلُوا۟ صَٰلِحًا إِنِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ

> **21:80** وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَٰكِرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (34:10): God softened iron for Dawud.

**c2** (34:11): He was told to make sabighat, a word for things made full and ample, and to measure well the links, and those addressed were told to do righteous deeds, because God sees what they do.

**c3** (21:80): God taught him the craft of making labus, a covering, to protect people in their fighting, and asked whether they would then be thankful.

### One-minute summary

God softened iron for Dawud and taught him a craft of making protection, and asked whether people would be thankful [c1][c3].

### Complete story

God softened iron for Dawud [c1]. He was told to make sabighat, a word for things made full and ample, and to measure well the links, and those addressed were told to do righteous deeds, because God sees what they do [c2]. God taught him the craft of making labus, a covering, to protect people in their fighting, and asked whether they would then be thankful [c3].

### Deep study

The ayat use different words for what was made: sabighat and the links (sard) in 34:11, and labus in 21:80 [c2][c3]. Neither ayah uses the word armour [c2][c3]. The ayat end with a call to righteous deeds in 34:11 and with a question about thanks in 21:80 [c2][c3].

### Kids mode

God made iron soft for Dawud [c1]. God taught him to make something that protects people, and asked if they would be thankful [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): In 21:80 a skill is given as a benefit for others, and it is followed by a question about thanks [c3]. In 34:11 the instruction to work with care is joined to an instruction to do righteous deeds [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how the iron was softened, or how the craft was carried out.
- Not established: what exactly sabighat and labus were; later commentators commonly read them as protective gear for battle, but the ayat do not use that word.
- Not established: who is meant by the people to be protected and the people asked about thanks in 21:80.

## 5. The judgment about the field  (`#the-field-judgment`)

Cited ayat: 21:78-79

> **21:78** وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ
>
> **21:79** فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (21:78): Dawud and Sulayman were judging about the field, when the sheep of some people had pastured in it by night, and God was a witness to their judgment.

**c2** (21:79): God made Sulayman understand it, and to each of them God gave judgment and knowledge.

### One-minute summary

Dawud and Sulayman judged about a field in which some people's sheep had pastured by night, and God made Sulayman understand it [c1][c2].

### Complete story

Dawud and Sulayman were judging about the field, when the sheep of some people had pastured in it by night, and God was a witness to their judgment [c1]. God made Sulayman understand it, and to each of them God gave judgment and knowledge [c2].

### Deep study

The verse says that God made Sulayman understand it, and does not say what Dawud had judged or what Sulayman judged [c2]. The same verse says that to each God gave judgment and knowledge [c2].

### Kids mode

Dawud and Sulayman judged a matter about a field and some sheep [c1]. God helped Sulayman understand it, and gave judgment and knowledge to both [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Sulayman's understanding is described as something God gave, and the same verse says that to each God gave judgment and knowledge [c2]. A reader may notice that the verse does not set one of them against the other [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what each of them judged, or which judgment is meant by it in 21:79.
- Not established: whose field or whose sheep, what damage was done, or whether the matter was brought to both of them together.
- Not established: Sulayman's age at the time; the Quran does not give it.

## 6. The disputants who came to Dawud  (`#the-two-disputants`)

Cited ayat: 38:21-25

> **38:21** وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا۟ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
>
> **38:22** إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
>
> **38:23** إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِى لَهُۥ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِىَ نَعْجَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلْخِطَابِ
>
> **38:24** قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِى بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَّا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًا وَأَنَابَ
>
> **38:25** فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍ

### Claims

**c1** (38:21): The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants had reached the one addressed, when they climbed into the mihrab.

**c2** (38:22): They went in to Dawud and he was alarmed at them; they said not to fear, that they were disputants who had transgressed against one another, and asked him to judge between them with the truth, not to be unjust, and to guide them to the middle of the path.

**c3** (38:23): One of them said that this was his brother, that the brother had ninety-nine ewes and he himself had one ewe, and that the brother had said to entrust her to him and had overcome him in speech.

**c4** (38:24): Dawud said that he had wronged him by asking for his ewe in addition to his own ewes, and that many partners transgress against one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they.

**c5** (38:24): The ayah says that Dawud thought that God had only tested him, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned back.

**c6** (38:25): God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness with Him and a good place of return.

### One-minute summary

Some disputants came into Dawud's mihrab, and one told of a brother with ninety-nine ewes while he had one [c2][c3]. Dawud thought that God had tested him, asked forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned back, and God forgave him that and spoke of his nearness and good return [c5][c6].

### Complete story

The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants had reached the one addressed, when they climbed into the mihrab [c1]. They went in to Dawud and he was alarmed at them [c2]. They said not to fear, that they were disputants who had transgressed against one another, and asked him to judge between them with the truth, not to be unjust, and to guide them to the middle of the path [c2]. One of them said that this was his brother, that the brother had ninety-nine ewes and he himself had one ewe, and that the brother had said to entrust her to him and had overcome him in speech [c3]. Dawud said that he had wronged him by asking for his ewe in addition to his own ewes, and that many partners transgress against one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they [c4]. The ayah says that Dawud thought that God had only tested him, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned back [c5]. God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness with Him and a good place of return [c6].

### Deep study

The news is introduced as a question to the one addressed (38:21) [c1]. The disputants' words set one with many ewes against one with a single ewe [c3]. Dawud's reply adds a general remark about partners [c4]. The ayah calls what happened a test, using the verb fatana, and does not say what the test was or draw a conclusion from it [c5]. It then says that God forgave him that and that he has nearness and a good place of return [c6].

### Kids mode

Some people came to Dawud with an argument [c2]. One of them said that his brother had ninety-nine ewes and he had one [c3]. Dawud asked God to forgive him, and God forgave him [c5][c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat show the one who judges turning back to God and asking forgiveness [c5]. They also show God answering with forgiveness and with words of nearness [c6]. A reader may take from Dawud's remark that those who join together can transgress against one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the disputants were, how they came in, or where the mihrab was; the ayat give no names or places.
- Not established: what the test was, what that refers to in the forgiveness of 38:25, or whether any wrong was done; the ayat give no verdict and this draft gives none.
- Not established: whether brother in 38:23 means kinship or companionship, or whether the ewes stand for something else.
- Not established: who is the speaker in 38:24, since the verb has no named subject; this draft reads it as Dawud, and the reviewer decides.
- Not established: whether fell down bowing means a bow or a prostration (the Arabic is kharra raki'an).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: accounts that explain the test, including identities for the disputants and their dispute; none is used here and none is vouched for.

## 7. A trust on the earth  (`#a-trust-on-the-earth`)

Cited ayat: 38:26

> **38:26** يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةً فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌۢ بِمَا نَسُوا۟ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ

### Claims

**c1** (38:26): God told Dawud that He had made him a khalifah on the earth, a word whose sense is left open, so he should judge between people with the truth.

**c2** (38:26): He was told not to follow desire, which would lead him astray from God's way; those who go astray from God's way have a severe punishment because they forgot the day of reckoning.

### One-minute summary

God told Dawud that He had made him a khalifah on the earth, to judge between people with the truth and not to follow desire [c1][c2].

### Complete story

God told Dawud that He had made him a khalifah on the earth, a word whose sense is left open, so he should judge between people with the truth [c1]. He was told not to follow desire, which would lead him astray from God's way [c2]. Those who go astray from God's way have a severe punishment because they forgot the day of reckoning [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah is a direct address to Dawud by name [c1]. It joins an appointment, a command to judge with the truth, and a warning in a single verse [c1][c2].

### Kids mode

God told Dawud to judge between people with the truth [c1]. He was told not to follow his own wishes, which could lead him away from God's way [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayah ties a position on the earth to the duty of judging with the truth [c1]. It names following desire as a way that leads away from God's way [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what khalifah means here, whether successor, steward or something else; the same word is used of humankind in 2:30 and the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: whom Dawud succeeded, if the word means successor, or over whom he judged.
